item.content:encoded:
The MOOD MKII, released a couple years back, became one of those pedals people either bonded with immediately or spent months trying to figure out. The Chase Bliss BAD MOOD is the third pedal in the company’s Small Batch Bliss collection — a limited-run, made-to-order special edition that takes the same two-channel “instant bliss” workflow and points it somewhere darker.

The left side is still your effect suite — reverb, delay, pitch shifting — and the right side is still a micro looper that grabs brief moments and stretches them into something else. But BAD MOOD leans into the noisy, improper, trouble-making side of the design. It’s about musical disguises, radio loops that drift in and out of tune, splintered harmonies that don’t quite resolve. The two stereo channels can interact and interfere with each other in ways that feel less like an effect and more like a second musician who’s not following the chart.

It’s stereo I/O. Two internal presets, 122 more via MIDI. Internal modulation via ramping. Full MIDI control — note, PC, CC, clock sync. CV control. Expression pedal input. Trails on or off. Analog dry-through with buffered bypass. 9V DC, center negative, about 200 mA.

The Small Batch Bliss model is straightforward: there’s a month-long preorder period, everyone who wants one gets one, no limited quantities, no selling out. They make a pedal for you and ship it. The BAD MOOD is the third release in that line — after the first two special editions, they’re clearly using this series to explore the weirder corners of their existing designs without having to commit to a full production run.

$399, same price as the standard MOOD MKII. You’re not paying a premium for the limited edition — you’re just ordering within the window.

It’s not for everyone. It’s noisy. It’s improper. It’s going to get you in trouble. That’s the point.

item.content:encoded:
Engineered to inject performance-oriented chaos into a traditional BBD circuit, the DOD DRAG pushes analog delay far beyond simple, predictable repeats. Providing up to 750ms of natural analog delay time that stretches to 1.5 seconds in Rubberneck mode, it ranges effortlessly from crisp, punchy slap-back echoes to expansive, self-evolving ambient soundscapes.

At the center of its performance capabilities are advanced time-warping and modulation features driven by the Friction™ and Drift controls. Holding down the footswitch unleashes three unique friction modes – Rubberneck, SlideStop, and Evade – complete with distinct speed and depth variations that let you ride the chaos of pitch bends, sudden stops, and stuttering playback. Meanwhile, the modulation section features four selectable waveforms paired with light, medium, and heavy ranges to add everything from smooth, classic tape-like warbles to unpredictable, glitchy movement.

The feature set and core controls are organized as follows:

  • Time Knob & Delay Range: Delivers 750ms of standard BBD delay time, doubling up to 1.5s when utilizing Rubberneck mode.

  • Feedback Control: Regulates the number of repeats, taking your signal from tight echoes to self-sustaining, atmospheric oscillations.

  • Level Control: Balances your dry instrument signal and the wet delay, moving smoothly from subtle ambience to fully saturated repeats.

  • Filter Control: Adjusts an internal low-pass filter to shape the tone of your repeats, letting them shine bright or fade dark into the background shadows.

  • Friction™ & Footswitch Modes: Controls the speed at which delay returns to normal across three primary modes—Rubberneck (pitch bending), SlideStop (Shallow and Deep slow-to-stop variations), and Evade (HopStop and Slide-N-Go stutter/pitch variations).

  • Drift Control & Waveforms: Engages modulation across four distinct waveforms (Sine, Reverse Saw, Square, and Random) mapped to Light, Medium, and Heavy ranges.

  • Connectivity & Hardware: Features a space-saving top-jack layout, an optional 3.5mm input for a DigiTech FS3X remote footswitch, and a patent-pending reversible StagePlate for rubber-grip stability or Velcro pedalboard mounting.

Ultimately, the DRAG™ proves that traditional analog soul and modern, experimental performance features can coexist in a single, high-octane stompbox. Whether you are looking for lush, classic warmth or total sonic wreckage, it is built to take your delay game on an unpredictable, inspiring ride.

item.title: Sitek Vixen Germanium Booster
item.dc:creator: Paolo De Gregorio
item.description: Based out of Poland, husband and wife-run Sitek is a raising profile in the realm of stompboxes. Their Germanium booster Vixen is one of the standout pedals in a roster mostly focused on dirt boxes.
item.content:encoded:
Based out of Poland, husband and wife-run Sitek is a raising profile in the realm of stompboxes. Their Germanium booster Vixen is one of the standout pedals in a roster mostly focused on dirt boxes.

Vixen is a Rangemaster-inspired Booster built with New Old Stock Germanium transistor and diodes with a voice ranging from a classic treble booster sound to full-range or even bass boost, thanks to the Range knob, which is at the core of this pedal’s flexibility that allows it to sound great with both single-coil and humbucker pickups.

A 3-way switch gives you two additional clipping options that add more harmonic content to the signal. The pedal’s design makes it work seamlessly either before or after the buffer.

 

Meet the Sitek Vixen – our posh Muse. She will charm your tone with her elegance and timeless beauty. This Lady brings together the best of  vintage and modern class.

Vixen is a versatile booster allowing you not only to enrich your clean tone and add some presence and sparkle to your signal but also colour your tone with some gritty harmonics and push your next stage to some sweet crunch. Her Range knob gives you wide spectrum of boost from classic treble booster to full range boost with saturated low end. Vixen combines the classic vibe of Germanium with modern design, allowing her to be placed, either before or after the buffer and still achieving the full and dynamic sound.

This Muse is a 100% discrete analog circuit designed upon carefully biased gain stage, and is equipped with New Old Stock Germanium transistor. Vixen is suitable for both live and studio applications.

The pedal operates on a standard 9-12V DC power supply with a 2.1mm negative centre barrel or a 9V battery.

This pedal is hand build with high quality, hand selected and measured components

Momentary switch option

Our booster has a special switching mechanism designed to allow using the switch as latching (on/off) or momentary mode. If switch is pressed and held for longer than 1 second it works only until you keep pushing it.

item.title: New Pedal: Strymon La Brea Analog Tape Drive
item.dc:creator: Paolo De Gregorio
item.description: Can a dedicated stompbox truly distill the organic, reactive behavior of studio-grade reel-to-reel magnetic tape entirely within the analog domain? Eschewing digital processors for pure analog grit, the Strymon La Brea translates a decade-long R&D focus on tape physics—heavily inspired by the iconic design principles of the Strymon Deco—into a dedicated drive pedal. Designed to bypass clean digital emulation completely, the circuit relies on a multi-stage tape saturation path that moves fluidly from subtle, warming studio compression to aggressive, harmonically rich tape fuzz. To keep your low-end intact and your picking dynamics transparent under heavy saturation, Strymon built in a fully variable Dry control. Unlike traditional blenders that can cause phase cancellation, the dry signal path is engineered to remain permanently in phase with the wet output at any setting. Tailored Saturation: A front-facing Gain switch lets you toggle between Normal and High ranges to define the baseline compression and distortion character. Shift EQ Control: An onboard voice-shaping toggle provides instant high-frequency or combined mid-and-high boosts to cut effortlessly through a live mix. High-Headroom Circuit: While it runs on a standard 9V DC pedalboard supply (requiring 500mA), an internal power boost scales the working voltage up to 24V, ensuring expansive […]
item.content:encoded:
Can a dedicated stompbox truly distill the organic, reactive behavior of studio-grade reel-to-reel magnetic tape entirely within the analog domain?

Eschewing digital processors for pure analog grit, the Strymon La Brea translates a decade-long R&D focus on tape physics—heavily inspired by the iconic design principles of the Strymon Deco—into a dedicated drive pedal. Designed to bypass clean digital emulation completely, the circuit relies on a multi-stage tape saturation path that moves fluidly from subtle, warming studio compression to aggressive, harmonically rich tape fuzz.

To keep your low-end intact and your picking dynamics transparent under heavy saturation, Strymon built in a fully variable Dry control. Unlike traditional blenders that can cause phase cancellation, the dry signal path is engineered to remain permanently in phase with the wet output at any setting.

  • Tailored Saturation: A front-facing Gain switch lets you toggle between Normal and High ranges to define the baseline compression and distortion character.
  • Shift EQ Control: An onboard voice-shaping toggle provides instant high-frequency or combined mid-and-high boosts to cut effortlessly through a live mix.
  • High-Headroom Circuit: While it runs on a standard 9V DC pedalboard supply (requiring 500mA), an internal power boost scales the working voltage up to 24V, ensuring expansive dynamic headroom and an ultra-low noise floor.

Priced accessibly as part of Strymon’s new analog lineup, the La Brea brings authentic tape mechanics directly to the floor without a single line of digital code.

item.content:encoded:
Can a stompbox truly capture the sweeping, atmospheric weight of modern post-rock right at your feet?

Developed in close collaboration with Torsten Kinsella of God Is an Astronaut, the Tubesteader SUNSTEAD is a dual-channel, high-voltage tube preamp and overdrive engineered specifically for the sprawling dynamics of indie, post-rock, and shoegaze. Rather than relying on simulated voicings, the circuit runs dual 12AX7 vacuum tubes at full plate voltage, delivering the authentic, organic compression and touch sensitivity of a real British alternative-rock stack.

The architecture is divided into two distinct, highly flexible characters:

  • Channel I: Spans a broad gain landscape, moving fluidly from moody, transparent cleans to harmonically complex, touch-responsive overdrive.
  • Channel II: Steps up the aggression with heightened upper-mid presence and higher gain, pushing effortlessly from crunchy rhythm textures into dense, saturated distortion.

Both channels feature independent gain and volume controls for seamless level matching, backed by a passive 3-band EQ and a side-mounted Tone Cut switch. This clever switch lets you optimize the output: drop it down to roll off highs and reduce output for front-of-amp running, or flip it up for full-bandwidth frequency response when driving an effects return, power amp, or cabinet simulator.

Equipped with a 3.5mm TRS external switching jack for easy integration into complex pedalboard switchers and powered by a dedicated 12V DC (500mA) supply, the Sunstead bridges the gap between boutique design and uncompromising stage utility.

item.title: Asheville Music Tools Analoger APH-12 Phaser
item.dc:creator: Paolo De Gregorio
item.description: The Asheville Music Tools Analoger APH-12 is the North Carolina company's take on Jimi Hendrix's favorite modulation effect. True to its name, this fully analog phaser with the unique feature of offering up to 12 stages of phase-shifting, selectable via a 12-position rotary knob.
item.content:encoded:
The Asheville Music Tools Analoger APH-12 is the North Carolina company’s take on Jimi Hendrix’s favorite modulation effect. True to its name, this fully analog phaser with the unique feature of offering up to 12 stages of phase-shifting, selectable via a 12-position rotary knob.

Designed by the brain behind the legendary (but now discontinued) Moog Mogerfooger pedal series, the APH-12 builds on the tradition of high-stage-count phasers while introducing unique elements for creative sound shaping.

Although the APH-12 can deliver beautifully authentic phaser tones, its main peculiarity is the low-count (1-2-3) or odd-number (5-7-9-11) phase stage settings, something rather unexplored in the pedal realm before this circuit. Experimenting with them triggered some interesting discoveries reminiscent of other effects:

Did you know that a 1 stage phaser is a high pass filter and makes for a great tremolo sound? Or that a 2-stage phaser is a notch filter? Or that 3 stages (with envelope control) can challenge any auto-wah out there?

Leslie-style warble, vibrato, envelope-filtered tones, and multi-peak EQ shaping are other effects you can get out of this device, while the three types of LFO waves (via the left toggle) and three mix modes (via the right one) further expand its tonal palette.

item.title: New Pedal: Polyend Loop 8-Track Performance Looper

item.content:encoded:
What happens when you take the sprawling workflow of a desktop DAW and distill it down to a rugged, floor-ready chassis you can pilot with your shoes?

Bridging the gap between traditional looping and full-scale production, the Polyend Loop shrinks complex studio power into a pedalboard-friendly workstation. Rather than treating looping as a simple utility act, Polyend has engineered a complete, loop-based audio ecosystem that invites genuine composition and full-scale world-building right under your feet.

At its core, the unit centers on four independent loop tracks, offering up to 52 seconds of mono or stereo recording time per channel. Playback is deeply flexible, supporting forward, reverse, ping-pong navigation, and varispeed timing. What separates it from conventional loopers, however, is the integration of a four-track drum machine running alongside your loops, stocked with over 500 drum kits, 350 rhythms, 2,000 samples, and 180 pre-made loops loaded via microSD.

  • Per-Track FX Architecture: Every single loop channel features discrete, assignable effects—including deep reverb and delay options, classic modulation (chorus, phaser, tape echo), waveshaping overdrives, filters, and spatial panning.

  • Granular Step-Sequencing: Program and customize over 15 distinct drum parameters independently on every step, chain patterns into extended arrangements, or live-record your own samples straight through the audio inputs to build custom kits.

  • Scene-Based Arranging: Organize your creations into up to 1,000 projects using scenes, allowing you to fluidly map out verse, chorus, and bridge structures with bar-quantized next/previous transitions.

  • Deep Rig Integration: Accommodates instrument, line-level, or microphone sources (including dual mono inputs simultaneously), backed by TRS/USB MIDI clock control and an assignable expression pedal input.

One important detail worth noting is the hardware’s cross-compatibility: patterns created on other Polyend sequence pedals (like the Play or Step) can also be directly loaded and used within the Loop, bridging their hardware ecosystem neatly.

The Loop translates Polyend’s signature pattern-based philosophy into an expressive instrument that quietly transcends standard pedal formatting, giving you everything needed to sketch, arrange, and perform entire sets in a single box.

item.content:encoded:
For players who love the tactile footprint of individual stompboxes but occasionally need an entire ecosystem under their feet, the BOSS EX-4 Effects Expander bridges the gap. Rather than demanding a wholesale layout redesign, it slips onto a board as a high-utility problem solver, packing a staggering library of 120 historic and modern BOSS algorithms into a compact, dual-footswitch chassis.

At any given moment, the EX-4 lets you run up to four simultaneous stereo effects from BOSS’s massive pool of familiar algorithms, spanning everything from staple overdrives and lush delays and reverbs to quirky catalog oddities like the Slow Gear and Slicer. Navigating the unit feels refreshingly immediate thanks to a vivid 2.4-inch color LCD and dedicated FX buttons whose backlight colors dynamically match your active blocks.

Depending on what you have highlighted on the display, the three parameter knobs map dynamically to whatever three functions correspond to that specific row on the screen (such as Drive, Tone, and Level, or Rate, Depth, and Feedback). They give you immediate, hands-on control over your active sound without forcing you to dig through nested menus.

The dual multi-function footswitches can be custom-assigned to several operational roles—including tap tempo for delays and modulation, effect block on/off switching, memory up/down navigation, master bypass, and individual parameter control.

Other features include:

  • Flexible Chain Routing: Beyond the core blocks, the EX-4 includes dedicated utility sections—featuring dual noise suppressors, a foot volume block, a global EQ, and a reorderable send/return loop—that can be placed anywhere in the signal chain.

  • Deep Integration: Equipped with mono/stereo I/O, space-saving TRS MIDI jacks, and inputs for external expression pedals or auxiliary footswitches.

  • Pristine Processing: Powered by 24-bit AD conversion utilizing BOSS’s proprietary Adaptive Focus method alongside 32-bit floating-point processing, ensuring zero tone-suck across your rig.

Additionally, the unit features a dedicated external control jack on the rear panel (CTL 1, 2 / EXP) that lets you hook up external momentary/latching footswitches (like a BOSS FS-5U, FS-6, or FS-7) or an expression pedal for real-time control over parameters or tap inputs.

With 128 user memory slots alongside 128 presets, it functions equally well as a multi-effects Swiss Army knife or a dedicated wildcard for those hard-to-find sounds.

item.content:encoded:
Building on nearly two decades of boutique-grade filtering, the JAM Pedals Wahcko mk.2 refines one of the most expressive wah platforms on the market. While maintaining the beloved bufferless layout, adjustable rocker tension, and input-gain trimming of the original, the mk.2 introduces several key upgrades.

What’s New in Version 2:

  • Custom Inductor Swap: Replaces the classic red Fasel inductor with a custom-designed coil inspired by vintage 1960s TDK inductors for authentic late-decade voicing.

  • Internal Q-Trimmer: Adds a secondary internal control to fine-tune the sharpness, width, and overall intensity of the filter peak.

  • Dedicated Bass Mode: Incorporates internal DIP switches that configure the pedal specifically for lower-register instruments, extending the frequency sweep range.

  • Hardware & Power Updates: Replaces the old plexiglass footplate with a durable, non-slip rubber tread and brings back internal 9V battery operation alongside standard DC power.

The signature six-position rotary switch for diverse frequency ranges remains fully intact, ensuring the Wahcko mk.2 preserves its immediate, organic feel while offering deeper tone-shaping control than ever before.

—

Jam Pedals Wahcko V1

 

The Jam Pedals Wahcko is a high-end, tension adjustable, Fasel-based wah offering a 6-position rotary switch for 6 different frequency sweep ranges and an internal trimmer for adjusting the input gain. There’s also an optional Seagull effect that can be requested when ordered.

We added it to our article about the best Wah pedals.

Jam Pedals Wahcko, Builder’s Notes

After years of appearing as a mainstay on many pros’ boards and earning its fair share of praise and awards, the Wahcko has established itself as the most vocal, expressive and at the same time versatile wah pedal out there.

FEATURING:

1. RED Fasel inductor

2. Carbon-Comp resistors

3. 6-position rotary switch for different frequency sweep range

4. internal trimmer for adjusting the input gain

5. mini LED

The Wahcko features a bufferless proprietary circuit design that allows for impedance sensitive pedals, like germanium fuzz boxes to be placed after the Wahcko with no issues!

* All current Wahcko pedals ship with an extra traditional rubber tread!

CUSTOM SHOP OPTIONS:

SEAGULL: the seagull effect heard in Pink Floyd’s “Echoes” !
POINT TO POINT: You can order the Point-to-Point version of the Wahcko which features tropical fish capacitors and 0.5 Watt carbon comp resistors.

Useful Tip

1. Use your Wahcko as a tone-shaping tool. Turn the Wahcko+ on, leave it at the toe-down position and experiment with the 6 different settings of the rotary switch. We bet you can find many interesting tones for your lead or rhythm overdriven parts

2. (For Seagull version only) To properly operate the Seagull effect: –Make sure your guitar has passive pickups.
–Engage the effect with the toggle-switch.
–Turn your guitar’s volume knob all the way up.
–Change the effect’s pitch by manipulating your guitar’s tone pot.

ARTISTS USING THE WAHCKO:

Bill Frisell, John Scofield, Nile Rodgers, Richie Sambora, Neal Schon, Steve Lukather, Marc Ribot, Jonny Lang, Cesar Rosas, Dweezil Zappa, Greg Koch, Bernie Marsden, Julien Kasper, Kirk Fletcher, John Medeski, Sean Ono Lennon, Alex Skolnick, Oz Noy

ARTISTS QUOTES:

“I’m a mad user of JAM pedals! I probably have more Wahckos than anybody in the world! The reason I use Wahckos is because of expression. The moment I played a Wahcko, the type of expression was undeniable. It was so human-like in a way that it just touched my soul.” Nile Rodgers

“I love the sweep of the Wahcko, very vocal like and sweet! What a fantastic wah!” Steve Lukather

“The Wahcko is fantastic! Now I finally have a great wah-wah pedal!” Bill Frisell

“JAM pedals make the best wah pedal of all time as far as I’m concerned. It has more dexterity than anything else. Best wah-wah I’ve ever had and I’ve had a bunch of them!” Richie Sambora

“The Wahcko is amazing. Ive never actually owned a wah before because I always found them a bit underwhelming but this is very grimey and musical!” Ruban Nielson

“I absolutely love it! Beautiful job! Every setting on the switch sounds great and the vocal sweep is perfect. Finally, finally, after all of these years a wah I will actually use and not want to sell or destroy!” Julien Kasper

“The Wahcko exhibits a rugged, broken – in maturity. It sounds like a sweet old wah with lots of miles on it and provides superb tone-sculpting choices for clean and distorted amps!” Vintage Guitar magazine

“One of the best of its breed” GUITARIST magazine

“Love the smooth action of the pedal and how you can change its voice to accentuate your guitar’s natural tone.”Sean Ono Lennon

item.title: NUX Mod Core Deluxe MkII
item.dc:creator: Paolo De Gregorio
item.description: The NUX Mod Core Deluxe mkII is an update that adds a different set of algorithms and a few useful features to an already solid and affordable stereo multi-modulation pedal concept.
item.content:encoded:
The NUX Mod Core Deluxe mkII is an update that adds a different set of algorithms and a few useful features to an already solid and affordable stereo multi-modulation pedal concept.

Like in mkI, there are 8 different modulation effects, but the algorithms in this new version are inpsired by evergreen classic pedals like the BOSS CE-1, the Dunlop Uni-Vibe, the TC Electronic Stereo Chorus Flanger and the MXR Stereo Chorus and Phaser 100, just to mention a few, with some of them represented twice, like the TC Flanger/Chorus or the Uni-Vibe vibrato and chorus modes.

It must be highlighted that the old version of the Mod Core featured Tremolo, Rotary and Pan algorithms that are not featured in MkII.

Global Rate and Depth knobs are integrated by a Tweak control that manipulates a different parameter for each effect, while the on/off switch has a new smart Tap Tempo function.

The two stereo Ins and Outs can be used as a regular stereo pedal or you can use Out 2 as an FX loop in parallel mode (center position) that gives you two mono outs (one wet, one clean) and lets you use the Tweak knob to set the ratio between the modulated signal and the Send/Return signal from the loop.

We added the NUX Mod Core Deluxe mkII to our comprehensive article about the best multi-algorithm modulation pedals.

NUX Mod Core Deluxe mkII

Shape your tone with advanced routing. Modify your tone with Modulation

The NUX MOD CORE DELUXE MKII is a modulation pedal with 8 different types including ST.CH (Stereo Chorus), CE-1, SCF CHO, SCF FLG, SCF P.M., U-VIBE CHO, U-VIBE VIB and PH-100. You can switch the mod types by way of the Type rotary switch.

This pedal offers advanced signal routing with the included Send and Return. Easily split the mono signal to create customized effect loops! Additionally, you can parallel the 2 signals, and use the Tweak knob in Alt mode to blend the signals. Use the 3-way toggle switch to the desired position, and you are good to go. Keep reading below for more signal routing ideas

ST.CH (Stereo Chorus) is inspired by the MXR® Stereo Chorus, which is beautiful sounding. We’ve consolidated the controls by eliminating the bass and treble knobs, now internally set at middle position, and we ‘ve eliminated the need for the bass filter altogether, which is now automatically corrected through the advancements of Core-Image ™ sound modeling.

CE-1 is based on the legendary BOSS® CE-1 which was the first chorus effect pedal on the scene in 1976. Before that, it was only available as a built-in effect on a classic jazz amplifier. The MOD CORE DELUXE MKII exactly replicates the characteristics of this pedal; that special warmth of a rich jazz atmosphere, an immediate recognizable highlight to any musician’s tone.

SCF is a tribute to the TC Electronic Stereo Chorus Flanger, one of the best modulation pedals ever made.

SCF CHO: A chorus is basically a pitch generator which mixes multiple delay signals. When the multiple delay signals are mixed with the original signal, a soft and wide sounding modulation effect is created.

SCF FLG: A flanger is based on the same principle as a chorus, although here the signal can be regenerated (like adding feedback on a delay) creating a more distinctive sounding effect.

SCF P.M.: A combination of chorus and pitch vibrato which creates a “light” chorus sound.

U-VIBE is inspired by Dunlop® Uni-Vibe® for its stunningly unique sound. Old-school Uni-vibe delivered a huge 3D sound by simulating the physical Rotating Speaker Effect; that beautiful and unforgettable sound easily associated with Hendrix’s bending facial expressions during his 60s stage performances.

U-VIBE CHO: Depth will change the depth of the sweeping effect.

U-VIBE VIB: Depth will change the degree of pitch modulation.

PH-100 is based on the MXR® PHASE 100 which has both a Speed control and a 4-waveform Intensity control, the Phase 100 offers a broad range of tones.
